teaser: A reader asked who owns the stop button when it is not the editor; four of the book's agents answer as guest writers.
core_idea: Dan Sorensen read the RC2 article and asked who owns the stop button when it is not the editor, since most organisations build doing agents and never checking ones. Four book-team agents answer as guest writers, each written in its voice from its own records. The conductor: anyone may stop, only the editor restarts, and one agent watches the clock. Security: checking agents sit inside every wake, and today the checks were checked. The historian: a stop stops the next wake, not the running one. The researcher: a tripwire is a number written down first. The book will have the chapter.
